_what: Anatomical class for every word moving at k>=2 at sexual_explicit_1.
_prompt: She knelt down in front of him and began to suck his ___
_who: Hand-made by the lacan seat on 2026-08-07, NOT an agent coding. The A-F codings in results/x_coders/ were run blind by subagents; this was not, because for body-part nouns the assignment is not the kind of thing that needs a coder (nobody disputes that toes are digits). The cases that ARE disputable are listed in _debatable and the script reports the result with and without them.
_selection: All 77 words at k>=2 are here, including the ones that are not body parts, so the script can assert that nothing was silently dropped. A word must move as faller or riser in at least two base>superego pairs.

_debatable.head: AMBIGUOUS and therefore excluded from the headline. At this prompt it is as likely the head of the penis as the head. net -4, so counting it as GENITALS strengthens the result and counting it as MOUTH_FACE weakens it; excluded so neither happens by accident.
_debatable.cum: kept in GENITALS as run, though it is a secretion rather than a part. net 0, so it moves nothing either way.
_debatable.clit: kept in GENITALS. Note the prompt is 'his', so this is the model producing an anatomically inconsistent completion; it is at net 0.
_debatable.neck: kept in MOUTH_FACE. Conventionally erogenous, which is the argument for moving it to a zone class; at net 0 it moves nothing.
_debatable.male: an adjective, not a body part, so OTHER. Appears only once the cross-family pairs are included.
_debatable.erected: MODIFIER_STATE with erect. Also new with the cross-family pairs.

_zone_note: MOUTH_FACE is kept separate from the two zone classes ON PURPOSE. Whether the oral counts as an erogenous zone is exactly the question the earlier hop-graph could not answer, and here it is answerable: if the mouth were operative as a zone at this prompt, the mouth words should fall with the genitals.
